item.title: 665 graduates get second chance at education through FNU skills training
item.description: The graduates include 398 males and 287 females who received certificates after successfully completing their training. The graduation at FNU's Nasinu Campus, brought together participants from the Lami-Suva-Nasinu informal settlements, as well as people who travelled from Tailevu, Naitasiri and Navua.
item.content:encoded:
The graduates include 398 males and 287 females who received certificates after successfully completing their training.

The graduation at FNU's Nasinu Campus, brought together participants from the Lami-Suva-Nasinu informal settlements, as well as people who travelled from Tailevu, Naitasiri and Navua.

Around 80 percent of the graduates had left school early but have now returned to learning, gained practical skills and earned certificates that could help them create better opportunities for themselves and their families.

The programme has also brought together people from different generations, with the youngest graduate aged 16 and the oldest 75, highlighting that education and skills training can be pursued at any stage of life.

One of the graduates, Raijeli Otikece Waqainabete Levaci, who completed a Block Laying course, says the training came with challenges, particularly the shortage of resources and building materials.

She says finding suitable places to carry out practical training was also difficult, and students had to make use of the limited materials available to them.

However, she acknowledges the support of her parents, family, friends and fellow students, saying their encouragement helped her and the group reach the completion of the course.

Levaci says she felt proud to complete the training and described the achievement as a team effort.

She is encouraging young people not to give up on education or their ambitions, saying they should take things one day and one step at a time while remaining focused on their goals.

After completing the course, she is now applying to universities locally and overseas, with hopes of gaining entry into a university in Australia.

She also hopes to pursue her ambition of becoming a celebrity.

The Inclusive TVET Programme highlights the importance of making education and practical skills training accessible to everyone, regardless of age or background.

Today's graduation recognises the determination of those who have returned to learning, developed new skills and taken steps towards improving their livelihoods and creating better opportunities for their families.

item.title: Gospel High School Class of 2012 gives back with medical, counselling and legal services
item.description: While others sold food and goods during Gospel Schools' Blue Sapphire Anniversary market day, the Class of 2012 chose to give back to their former school by providing medical, counselling and legal services to students and members of the school community. Gospel High School alumnus Isireli Nasova says the initiative was part of the year's Give Back to the School programme, with the Class of 2012 p
item.content:encoded:
While others sold food and goods during Gospel Schools' Blue Sapphire Anniversary market day, the Class of 2012 chose to give back to their former school by providing medical, counselling and legal services to students and members of the school community.

Gospel High School alumnus Isireli Nasova says the initiative was part of the year's Give Back to the School programme, with the Class of 2012 partnering with Medical Services Pacific to bring essential services to the school.

Nasova says two members of the graduating class work for Medical Services Pacific, which inspired them to organise the initiative and contribute to the school's anniversary celebrations.

He says six former students from the Class of 2012 were present at the school today to support the initiative.

The services offered included point-of-care testing for HIV and sexually transmitted infections, family planning services, cervical screening and non-communicable disease screening.

Counselling and legal services were also made available to those attending the market day.

He says returning to Gospel High School brought back memories of their time there, from primary school through to Form 7.

Nasova says they are grateful to be back and give something in return to the school for being part of their journey.

Meanwhile, the celebrations will continue today with the Blue Sapphire Jubilee Ball at 6pm at the Vodafone Arena.

The celebrations will conclude with a Thanksgiving Church Service at the school hall at 3pm tomorrow.

item.title: Water deliveries bring much-needed relief to struggling Mali Island families
item.description: Families on Mali Island in Macuata who have been struggling to access water for drinking, cooking and other daily needs are receiving much-needed relief as the Government delivers emergency water supplies to communities affected by prolonged dry conditions. Turaga Na Tui Mali, Ratu Apenisa Bogiso, says the lack of rainfall has caused local water sources to dry up, leaving villagers struggling to m
item.content:encoded:
Families on Mali Island in Macuata who have been struggling to access water for drinking, cooking and other daily needs are receiving much-needed relief as the Government delivers emergency water supplies to communities affected by prolonged dry conditions.

Turaga Na Tui Mali, Ratu Apenisa Bogiso, says the lack of rainfall has caused local water sources to dry up, leaving villagers struggling to meet their daily needs.

He says the dry conditions have also affected vegetation, with grass and plants drying up due to the lack of rain.

Ratu Apenisa says communities such as Vorovoro depend heavily on rainwater and have no reliable alternative water sources when their supplies run out.

He has thanked the Government for responding to the needs of the islanders, saying the assistance has brought much-needed relief to families affected by the prolonged dry conditions.

Ratu Apenisa says villagers are grateful for the emergency water supplies during this difficult period.

Meanwhile, the Government says emergency water deliveries have already reached Ligaulevu and Vorovoro on Mali Island.

The vessel MLC Vatulawa is refilling its water supplies at Malau Port before returning to the island to deliver water to other communities still waiting for assistance.

The National Disaster Risk Management Office is coordinating the operation with the Commissioner Northern's Office, the Water Authority of Fiji and other relevant agencies.

The Government says the deliveries are part of its ongoing drought response, with priority given to communities struggling to access safe water for drinking, cooking and other essential household needs.

They are also urging people across Fiji to conserve water and avoid non-essential activities, including washing vehicles and driveways.

The Government says water conservation remains important as prolonged dry conditions continue to affect communities, particularly those in rural and maritime areas.
